G1562798.description: Vinh (Vietnamese: [viŋ̟] ) is a former city located in the North Central Coast region of Vietnam and was the capital city of Nghệ An province, Vietnam. Vinh also is an economic and cultural center of the country's North-Central region.

G1563281.description: Tuy Hòa () is a coastal city and the former capital of the defunct Phú Yên province in the South Central Coast region of Vietnam. The city has a total area of 106.82 square kilometres or 41 square miles and a population of 155.921 (in 2019).

G1566083.description: Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC; Vietnamese: Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, [tʰaɲ˨˩ fow˦˥ ho˨˩ cɪj˦˥ mɨn˧˧] ), also known as Saigon (Sài Gòn, [ʂaj˨˩ ɣɔŋ˨˩]), is the most populous city and centrally-governed city of Vietnam, with a population of more than 14 million in 2025. Its geography is defined by rivers and canals, of which the largest is the Saigon River.

G1566166.description: Thanh Hóa (Vietnamese: [tʰajŋ̟ hwǎː] ) is the capital of Thanh Hóa Province. The city is situated in the east of the province on the Ma River (Sông Mã), about 150 kilometers (93 miles) south of capital Hanoi and 1560 kilometers (969 miles) north of Ho Chi Minh City.

G1566559.description: Tây Ninh () is a former provincial city and former capital of Tây Ninh province in Southeastern Vietnam. It is one of the cities in the Southern Key Economic Region (Ho Chi Minh City metropolitan area).

G1567788.description: Sóc Trăng (; Khmer: ស្រុកឃ្លាំង Srok Khleang lit. 'Land of depositories') is a city in Vietnam.

G1568510.description: Rạch Giá () is a provincial city and the former capital of Kiên Giang province, Vietnam. It is located on the Eastern coast of the Gulf of Thailand, 250 kilometres (160 mi) southwest of Ho Chi Minh City.

G1568574.description: Quy Nhon (Vietnamese: Quy Nhơn [kʷī ɲə̄ːŋ] ) was a former coastal city in Bình Định province in central Vietnam. It was composed of 16 wards and five communes with a total of 286 km2 (110 sq mi).

G1568770.description: Quảng Ngãi () is a city in central Vietnam. It serves as the capital city of Quảng Ngãi Province.

G1569684.description: Pleiku is a former city in central Vietnam, located in the Central Highlands region. It was the capital of the Gia Lai Province.

G1572151.description: Nha Trang (English: or ; Vietnamese: [ɲaː1 ʈaːŋ1] ) is a coastal city and the former capital of Khánh Hòa, on the South Central Coast of Vietnam. It was bounded on the north by the Ninh Hoà town, on the south by Cam Ranh city and on the west by Diên Khánh District.

G1573517.description: Nam Định (Vietnamese pronunciation: [naːm˧˧:ɗḭ̈ʔŋ˨˩]) was the capital city of Nam Định province in the Red River Delta of the Northern Vietnam. As part of the 2025 Vietnamese administrative reform, all district-level subdivisions, including Nam Định, were abolished.

G1580240.description: Huế (Vietnamese: [hwě] ) is a former provincial city of Vietnam. The city was the capital of Thừa Thiên Huế province in the North Central Coast region of Vietnam, located near the center of Vietnam.

G1580410.description: Hạ Long (Vietnamese: [hâːˀ lawŋm] , transl. 'descending dragon') is a former first-class provincial city and capital city of Quảng Ninh province, Vietnam. It was founded in 1993, when the old capital, Hòn Gai, was merged with Bãi Cháy, the main tourist area.

G1580541.description: Hội An (Vietnamese: [hoi˨˩ˀ an˧] ) is a former city of Quảng Nam Province in Central Vietnam. Hội An Old Town has been registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999 and is recognized as a well-preserved former site of a once-thriving Southeast Asian trading port dating from the 15th–19th century.

G1581047.description: Hà Tĩnh (Vietnamese: [hâː tǐŋ̟ˀ] ) is a city in Vietnam. It is the capital of Hà Tĩnh Province, and lies in the North Central Coast region.

G1581130.description: Hanoi ( ha-NOY; Vietnamese: Hà Nội, pronounced [haː˨˩ noj˧˨ʔ] ) is the capital and second-most populous centrally-governed city of Vietnam. It covers an area of 3,358.6 km2 (1,296.8 mi2), and as of 2025 has a population of 8,807,523.

G1582926.description: Đông Hà () is the capital of Quảng Trị Province, in the North Central Coast region, the Central of Vietnam. As of 2024, the city's population is approximately about 164,228 people.

G1583477.description: Điện Biên Phủ (Vietnamese: [ɗîənˀ ɓīən fû] , chữ Hán: 奠邊府) is a city in the northwestern region of Vietnam. It was the capital of Điện Biên Province before the 2025 Vietnamese administrative reform.

G1586185.description: Cao Bằng ([kāw ɓɐ̀ŋ] ) is a city in northern Vietnam. It is the capital and largest settlement of Cao Bằng Province.

G1586203.description: former city in Can Tho province, Vietnam

G1586443.description: Cà Mau () is a former city in southern Vietnam. It was the capital of Cà Mau province, a province in the Mekong Delta region, in the southernmost part of Vietnam's inland territory (mainland).

G1586896.description: Buôn Ma Thuột or sometimes Buôn Mê Thuột or Ban Mê Thuột (Vietnamese pronunciation: [ʔɓuon1 maː1 tʰuot̚ʔ6], ), is the capital city of Đắk Lắk Province in the Central Highlands of Vietnam. Its population was 434,256 in 2023.
